chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Sayābah, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

Indeed, in the book of ʿAlī عليه السلام, it is stated: “If a man were to sever a woman’s private part, I would make him liable to pay her its blood-money. Then if he did not pay her its blood-money, I would sever his private part for her, if she requested that.”

key_terms.دِيَتَهَا: Her blood-money compensation due for the injury
key_terms.طَلَبَتْ: She requested; indicating that enforcement depends on her demand
key_terms.فَرْجَ: The private part; here referring to the bodily organ subject to injury
key_terms.قَطَعْتُ: I would sever; here indicating retaliatory legal punishment
key_terms.كِتَابِ عَلِيٍّ: The written legal record attributed to Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام containing rulings
key_terms.يُؤَدِّ: To pay or discharge the financial liability owed

ai.seo_question: What does the Book of ʿAlī عليه السلام say about diyah and qisas for injuring a woman’s private part?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a legal ruling transmitted from the Book of ʿAlī عليه السلام concerning bodily injury and retaliation. It establishes the woman’s right to compensation through diyah, and if that is not rendered, it affirms the possibility of qisas upon her request.
